I will keep it simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the most reliable path for me is still the usual wheat and summer maize rotation on the same land. I know this system, I have the machinery for it, and it fits our water conditions and market habits better than trying something fancy. At the start of the season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I will push to manage it well through spring with fertilizer, one or two key irrigations, and disease control if pressure shows up. After wheat harvest, I will go straight into summer maize to protect the full-year output. I will use improved or hybrid seed, keep fertilizer at moderate but solid levels, avoid wasting water, and rely on rotary tillage because it is practical and cheaper for me than deep ploughing every time. My goal is stable yield and lower risk, not gambling on a crop I do not know as well.
